verdict.rationale: WezTerm provides the building blocks for background automation: a hands-on probe ran a fully headless loop with `wezterm-mux-server --daemonize`, then used `wezterm cli` to spawn, send-text, get-text and list panes with no GUI session. The docs confirm the cli subcommand can spawn programs and manipulate panes in a running mux instance. However, these are scripting primitives driven by an external tool, not a built-in way to define and run autonomous automations. Missing for 10: built-in scheduling or trigger mechanisms, first-party docs on setting up autonomous background workflows, and independent corroboration of such use.
